column3: Directly pairs the true judgment with the incapacity of those invoked apart from God.
Shows an answered invocation joined to a required straight course.
Adds an instance where an appeal receives effective help amid distress.
States that the alternative invoked has no effective call in either present or later horizon.
Extends the surah's challenge to named partners under comprehensive accountability.
Sets a contrary water outcome within the truth-and-consequence contrast.
Presents invocation and response as a reciprocal relation oriented toward right guidance.
Supplies the nearby frame of knowledge of hidden and visible matters.
Shows response to the divine call remaining active after injury.
Connects refusal to answer God's caller with manifest going-astray and no alternative protector.
Contributes the nearby warning-and-guidance frame without developing response.
Provides a secondary hand-extension image whose outcome is deliberately withheld.
Directly contrasts God as al-haqq with the falsehood of what is invoked apart from Him.
Explicitly forbids invoking another god alongside God.
Offers a secondary reach-and-route image, with arrival requiring continued movement.
Restates the al-haqq versus false-invocation contrast in a distinct setting.
Adds the surah's distinction between misdirection and return-guidance.
Supplies a secondary image of hands restrained; its rejected parallel should remain distinct.
Reuses the final formula that the invocation of the disbelievers is in going-astray.
Only broadens the local setting through hidden and open speech.
Offers a secondary arrival image where reaching a place does not ensure recognition.
Immediately develops response and non-response as a decisive local contrast.
Does not materially clarify invocation, response, truth, or the water comparison.
Supports the claim of true guardianship after false supports collapse.
Supplies a hearing-and-call failure that parallels unreceived invocation.
Adds a warning call to close kin but no response or false-invocation contrast.
The restraint image is too remote from the focus's call-and-water relation.
Reinforces the same conclusion about disbelieving plots being in going-astray.
Adds the local boundary that all command belongs to God, despite demanded signs.
Universal dispatch does not materially develop the focus's contrast.
Directly denies productive capacity to those invoked apart from God.
Adds punishment and lack of protection without clarifying the focus's mechanism.
Retains a secondary image of hostile hands being restrained.
Shows persistent calling in ease turning to despair under harm.
Places the focus after signs, contention, and divine force in the immediate passage.
Its rejected fertility parallel does not clarify the focus.
Challenges the claimed mediating role of protectors taken apart from God.
Most closely states the structural failure of calling one that never responds.
Privacy rules do not add to the focus's operative contrast.
Distinguishes the Messenger's summons from ordinary calls, but remains indirect.
The nearby neck-shackle image is not enough to interpret the water comparison.
Contributes only the broad association of al-haqq with distant going-astray.
Supports exclusive divine authority and knowledge, without the call-response structure.
Preserves a secondary open-hand image without resolving the focus's failed reach.
Does not add beyond the broad consequence for disbelief.
Shows a divine call producing an effective collective response.
Does not materially illuminate the focus's invocation contrast.
Affirms al-haqq but adds no call, response, or false target.
The isolated request for a clear thing is too slight a connection.
Supplies a nearby created-order setting, but not the focus's water relation.
Establishes the immediate water imagery and the al-haqq/al-batil distinction.
Offers only a remote water-source resonance.
Portrays a call that gathers dispersed people into response.
Supplies a secondary boundary of difficult speech and partial communication.
Shows a moral refusal that misuses divine will and culminates in manifest going-astray.
Adds a nearby water image of one source yielding differentiated outcomes.
Names God as the excellent responder to an invoked appeal.
Provides a contrary water scene where an assumed refuge fails.
Extends blindness into greater loss of the way, clarifying the force of dalal.
Its procedural boundary is too remote from the focus.
Distinguishes a false caller whose followers answered but who cannot help them.
Supplies the adjacent surah frame of al-haqq, sight, and blindness.
A relational condition of companionship does not add to the focus.
The trial list has no sufficiently specific link to the focus.
Maturity and judgment are too indirect a reach parallel.
Affirms a truthful message but does not clarify invocation or response.
Shows expansive calling under harm after turning away in ease.
Adds the nearby confession of exclusive lordship, reliance, and return.
Its geographical arrival and choice do not clarify the focus.
Contrasts ineffective mouth-claims with speech that guides the way.
Directly joins answering the distressed caller, removing harm, and exclusive divinity.
The waiting term does not materially contribute to the focus.
The isolated account of arrogance adds no specific interpretive value.
Shows worship diverted to a subordinate object and the consequent blocked way.
Clarifies message delivery as an obligation reaching its required extent.
Adds a secondary hand image after collapse and a rejection of association.
Keeps the immediate rain-and-signs setting in view before the focus.
Offers a secondary pattern of rejecting a confirming al-haqq.
Supplies a contrary water appeal whose requested water is withheld.
Divine measure and hidden gestation do not materially clarify the focus.
Retains a secondary extended-hands image amid false claims, but remains remote.
The promised claims do not develop the call-and-response contrast.
Separates the Messenger's delivery from God's accounting in the local surah context.
Truth knowingly concealed is only a broad secondary resonance.
Contrasts attempted suppression by mouths with God's completion of His light.
Adds local responsive conduct, but no direct invocation contrast.
Makes non-response to a challenge evidentiary against a rival claim.
Reiterates the mouth-and-light contrast already supplied by the earlier parallel.
Supports al-haqq through converging evidence, without a direct call-response scene.
Supplies a water-to-life scene that broadens, but does not duplicate, the water motif.
Reinforces divine permission and true judgment after stronger earlier parallels.
Shows argument continuing after response as groundless and collapsing.
The bare presentation of Hell adds no specific interpretive relation.
Contrasts emphatic denial with a promise characterized as al-haqq.
Maintains exclusive worship, but offers little on invocation's failure or response.
Supplies a secondary terminal-reach image at the throat.
Uses reaching an appointed endpoint procedurally, a distant route parallel.
Frames narrated account as bil-haqq, but lacks the focus's call relation.
Inheritance allocation does not materially clarify the focus.
Adds a bounded-knowledge account of losing the way, after more direct dalal cards.
Uses a summons to alleged witnesses apart from God, testing a rival claim by response.
Provides a direct personal invocation directed to God.
Joins hearing a caller with answering in faith.
Connects return, seeking forgiveness, and finding God responsive.
Explicitly identifies invocations apart from God with a false hostile source.
Rejects association in worship and grounds exclusive devotion to God.
Denies harm-benefit capacity to what is worshipped apart from God.
Tests distress by asking whether any other is invoked when the matter is true.
Makes exclusive calling on God the operative response to distress.
Forbids following those invoked apart from God.
Shows calling God sincerely from acute peril.
Identifies God as the rescuer from that peril and from every distress.
Questions calling what neither benefits nor harms apart from God.
Preserves the social reality of rival invocation while regulating its treatment.
Challenges those invoked apart from God to answer a call.
Details the incapacity of rival objects to respond or help.
States that those invoked apart from God cannot help either caller or themselves.
Shows exclusive, sincere calling on God when danger closes in.
Forbids calling what cannot benefit or harm apart from God.
States that no one but God can remove harm or withhold His good.
Shows invoked gods failing to avail their followers at judgment.
Extends the surah's exclusive-authority argument through paired contrasts.
Names God as one who hears invocation.
Records the collapse of a claim that partners had been invoked apart from God.
Directly denies that claimed beings can remove or transfer harm.
Shows all other invoked beings disappearing from view during danger at sea.
Affirms legitimate invocation through God's names without multiplying gods.
Depicts the calling of alleged partners and their failure to respond.
Separates devotion to God from calling what is apart from Him.
Shows withdrawal from rival invocation alongside exclusive worship.
Joins exclusive worship with remembrance through prayer.
Questions worship of what cannot benefit or harm.
Describes calling what can neither harm nor benefit as far-going error.
Exposes the invoked object as unable to supply the claimed support.
Denies even minimal creative capacity to all those invoked apart from God.
Rejects calling another god alongside God without proof.
Denies creative and self-directive power to objects taken apart from God.
Contrasts worship apart from God with the lack of benefit or harm.
Frames the question of what is worshipped before the incapacity argument unfolds.
Continues the surah's exclusive-divinity challenge through creation and guidance.
Calls alleged partners to account when they cannot answer.
Portrays the calling of alleged partners and their non-response.
Repeats the accounting summons to alleged partners.
Denies provision and creative authority to what is worshipped apart from God.
Denies intercessory support from alleged partners.
Challenges claimed beings apart from God as possessing no independent power.
Shows divine control of the cosmic order against alleged rival authority.
Most directly states that those invoked cannot hear or answer the call.
Rejects taking gods whose intercession cannot avail against divine harm.
Shows the futile expectation of help from gods taken apart from God.
Confronts claimed protectors with their inability before divine harm or mercy.
Challenges the taking of intercessors apart from God.
Directly promises a response to calling God and contrasts arrogant refusal.
States that God responds to those who believe and act rightly.
Restricts intercessory capacity among those invoked apart from God.
Challenges rival beings to show any share in creation or revealed warrant.
Shows supposed near gods failing to help those who took them.
Forbids calling anyone alongside God in places of worship.
States exclusive calling upon the Lord without association.
Denies personal control over harm and right guidance, sharpening dependence.
Denies any refuge from God apart from Him.
